stories.headline: State, UT-level Bankers’ Committees asked to report share of SC beneficiaries in jobs, loan subsidy schemes
stories.deck: Advisory comes after National Commission for SCs flagged that it was unable to monitor banks’ performance in the absence of such data in SLBC/UTLBC review reports
stories.bodyText:
The Finance Ministry has now directed State-level and Union Territory-level Bankers’ Committees to mandatorily include data on the percentage share of Scheduled Caste beneficiaries availing flagship Central schemes such as the Mudra Yojana, Stand Up India, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme, MSME/business loans, and others.
This direction comes after the National Commission for Scheduled Castes flagged the fact that these bankers’ committees were not reporting this data for a number of government schemes in their regular reviews, which was hindering the Commission’s ability to perform its Constitutional duties.
In a letter dated October 5, the Department of Financial Services of the Union Finance Ministry wrote to all State Level Bankers’ Committees (SLBCs) and Union Territory Level Bankers’ Committees (UTLBCs), asking them to include the percentage of SC beneficiaries for all the schemes flagged by the NCSC in their periodic reviews - both scheme-wise and bank-wise. The advisory also asked the bankers’ committees to ensure that this information is shared regularly with the Commission.
About a week ago, the NCSC had written to Sanjay Lohia, the Secretary of the Department of Financial Services (DFS), highlighting that in review meetings of the bankers’ committees, SLBC Conveners do not reflect the percentage of SC beneficiaries for several schemes meant to ensure financial inclusion of citizens.
In this letter, the NCSC noted that such data was missing for the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, Stand-Up India, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme, PM SVANidhi (Street Vendors’ scheme), Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises, and MSME business loans.
The Commission noted that its State Office representatives have been attending the bankers’ committee review meetings regularly to monitor the financial inclusion of SC families, as per its Constitutional mandate. Noting the absence of data on SC beneficiaries, the NCSC said, “It becomes very difficult for the Commission to review the performance of Banks, i.e. whether they have been extending help to the SC families as per the Constitutional mandate or not.”
Sources aware of these developments told The Hindu that in reviewing the banks’ performance, the Commission routinely checks whether the share of SC beneficiaries in these government schemes is as close as possible to the share of their communities in the population. “This has not been possible for the Commission in recent times because the bankers’ committees keep saying they do not have disaggregated data. This is why the Commission wrote to the DFS,” one government official said.
The DFS has now asked all SLBCs and UTLBCs to submit an action-taken report on the advisory issued to them by October 9, saying that any issues related to the availability of data should be flagged by this time. The bankers’ committees have further been told by the government to be prepared for an update on the action taken in a month’s time.

stories.headline: AI survey finds 14,000 potholes across North Bengaluru
stories.deck: AI survey finds 14k potholes across North Bengaluru
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: An Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based survey of roads in the Bengaluru North City Corporation has identified 14,393 potholes across 2,493.5 km of roads, even as the civic body has claimed that 82.1% of its road network is in “good to adequate” condition. . The ground reality in the other four corporations has also been more or less the same. The survey, conducted using real-time images captured through dashcams, covered all seven divisions and 72 wards of the corporation. It assessed road surface conditions, potholes, damaged stretches and roads affected by utility works. Other corporations have not shared the data yet. . Of the total road length surveyed, 1,426.8 km was classified as being in good condition, while another 607.1 km had minor surface defects. Together, these account for 82.1% of the road network. . The remaining 17.9% comprises stretches with localised damage, roads affected by utility works and unpaved or kuccha roads. The survey classified roads C0 to C4, with C0 representing the best condition and C4 the poorest. .Frustrated by inaction, youths fill potholes. The Byatarayanapura division, which has the largest road network at 823.5 km, recorded the highest number of potholes at 5,964. Sarvagnanagar, with 406.6 km of roads, had 2,359 potholes, followed by Hebbal (1,368), Pulakeshinagar (1,357), Rajarajeswari Nagar (1,222), Yelahanka (1,157) and Dasarahalli (966). . Overall, the survey has found an average of 5.8 potholes per kilometre. . The corporation said the AI-based survey would help it move away from a complaint-based approach to road maintenance and enable officials to prioritise repairs based on actual road conditions. The officials will use the survey data to identify potholes, surface defects, utility-related damage and unpaved roads and prioritise maintenance and development works, the corporation said.

briefs.headline: ASHAs can play greater role to fix mental health gaps: Study
briefs.deck: Study: ASHAs can play greater role to fix mental health gaps
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) in Karnataka could play a greater role in identifying and supporting people with mental-health conditions if they receive structured training to improve their knowledge and competencies, a systematic review has found. . The review by St John’s Medical School, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Research, examined studies on mental-health training and capacity-building interventions for ASHAs in Karnataka. Of 648 records screened, 13 studies involving 567 ASHAs met the inclusion criteria. . The researchers found structured training improved ASHAs’ mental-health knowledge and competencies, along with selected service-delivery outcomes like screening coverage, home visits and supervisory engagement. .ASHA workers in Karnataka stage protest seeking 5 months’ incentive. Digital and hybrid training models appeared to offer more sustained gains than standalone classroom-based training, highlighting the potential of technology-enabled approaches to train frontline health workforce. . The study says ASHAs are embedded within communities and can serve as a key link between people experiencing mental-health concerns and healthcare services. With good training, they can help identify symptoms, provide basic support, facilitate referrals and follow up with patients. . A Karnataka-based randomised controlled trial included in the review, tested an enhanced training model in which ASHAs received a one-day classroom session followed by seven online modules over 18 months. The training covered recognising mental illness, responding to suicidal thoughts, substance-use-related behavioural problems and referring people requiring specialised care. . Currently, there is one ASHA worker for every 1,000 people in rural areas and one for every 2,500 in urban areas. . The study also highlighted the potential for strengthening community-based mental-health services by building the capacity of an existing frontline workforce. . The lead researcher, Dr Johnson Pradeep, Head of Psychiatry Department, St John’s Medical College, said: “We are using a simple method and ASHAs are trained to spot symptoms for depression, anxiety, alcohol-related problem, suicide related issue and act as a bridge between patients and doctors.” . This will not be an extra burden of work, if they are screening for NCDs, mental health can also be screened. There is a manual for that but it is not being followed, he added. . Rithwik Ranjanam Pandey, Principal Secretary of Health Department, told DH: “In collaboration with Rotary Club, the department is planning to take up a pilot study in Anekal taluk to include mental health questionnaires in their routine screening. Unlike regular NCDs, follow-up for mental health is different and more complicated.” . Based on the results of the pilot study, the decision on implementation will be made, he added.

briefs.bodyText:
The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation’s (KSRTC) cargo service has made a strong debut, transporting one tonne of mobile phones from Thiruvananthapuram to Aluva in its inaugural consignment.
The consignment, flown from Delhi to Thiruvananthapuram International Airport by Air India, was transported to Aluva in a truck hired by the KSRTC. Transport Minister C.P. John flagged off the cargo service at a function held at the Thiruvananthapuram Domestic Airport cargo terminal in on Wednesday (October 7, 2026).
Five vehicles initially
Speaking after the inaugural function, the Minister said that this project, included in the government’s 100-day action plan, marked a significant milestone in KSRTC’s history. The cargo service, launching with five vehicles in the initial phase, would be expanded gradually. This new system would help strengthen KSRTC’s existing logistics network and boost non-ticket revenue, he said, adding that the KSRTC would eventually evolve to operate a large fleet comprising over a hundred trucks.
The KSRTC ventured into this sector after studying the successful cargo service models implemented by various State Road Transport Corporations across the country, as part of efforts to increase non-ticket revenue. The revenue generated from this initiative will be utilised in a manner that benefits KSRTC passengers. Currently, five trucks taken on a wet-lease basis are being used for the cargo operations.
The Minister said Scorpion Cart Logistics and Cargo Cart Logistics were providing support to KSRTC for this service.

briefs.headline: Brazilian students in Rio de Janeiro march against the prospect of another Bolsonaro presidency
briefs.deck: Thousands of Brazilian students have marched in Rio de Janeiro against the possibility of Flávio Bolsonaro winning the presidency
briefs.bodyText:
Thousands of Brazilian students marched in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to protest against the possibility of Flávio Bolsonaro winning the presidency, after the far-right candidate received more votes than incumbent and left-leaning Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election.
A sea of red-clad demonstrators made their way between two historical squares in Rio’s center, chanting and holding signs referencing Brazil’s sovereignty and democracy in the South American country, which they said were under threat.
“We’re fighting for Brazil, not for Lula,” said Talita Amaral, a 19-year-old environmental science student at a nearby university. She was wearing Brazil’s yellow and green soccer jersey, often worn by supporters of Bolsonaro, which she said was a gesture aimed at reclaiming the national colors.
“We don’t have time to be sad, we need to be doing this, occupying the streets, sending messages in WhatsApp groups, trying to convince people,” Amaral said, as the chant “Olé olé olé ola, Lula Lula” rang out across Cinelandia square.
Neither Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup, nor Lula received more than the required 50% of the vote needed to become Brazil’s leader on Sunday. Therefore, they will face each other in an unpredictable runoff on Oct. 25.
But Flávio Bolsonaro has at least two advantages: He received 2 million more votes than Lula on Sunday and the candidates who placed third, fourth and fifth are all on the right of the political spectrum. They gathered 6 million votes between them.
Mr. Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion because of his ties to the failed Banco Master — a case that many protesters in Rio made reference to on Wednesday.
Some pointed to Jair Bolsonaro's handling of the coronavirus pandemic, during which 700,000 people were reported to have died from the disease, while others held signs emblazoned with messages such as “Brazil isn't anyone's backyard” and “I don't vote for someone who sells Brazil.”
Many on the left fear a Flávio Bolsonaro presidency would fully align the Brazilian government with the United States because of the proximity in ideologies between U.S. President Donald Trump and the Bolsonaro family. Last year, Trump imposed a 50% tariff on Brazilian goods and imposed sanctions on a Brazilian Supreme Court justice, citing Jair Bolsonaro’s trial, which he called a “witch hunt.”
“If Bolsonaro wins, Brazil will become a colony of the United States,” said João Victor Vieira, 20, who studies literature. He said that Bolsonaro represented a threat to minorities such as people of color, women and the LGBTQ+ community. Bolsonaro's father was notorious for homophobic remarks.
Mr. Vieira said that while he was initially dispirited following the results on Sunday, he has since regained hope.
“This protest shows that social movements are still very much alive,” he said. “We will resist.”

stories.headline: No parent a visitor: Karnataka HC asks courts to use 'parenting time'
stories.deck: Karnataka high court has directed family courts to replace the term 'visitation' with 'parenting time' in custody orders. This change aims to improve how children perceive their relationships with non-custodial parents. The directive was issued during a custody case involving a nine-year-old boy and his father. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti made this observation to encourage a more positive…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The term "visitation" may soon be dropped from child custody orders in Karnataka. In an interim directive, Karnataka high court has asked all family courts and other courts hearing petitions under the Guardians and Wards Act (G&WC) to use the term "parenting time" instead, of "visitation" when referring to the time a child spends with the non-custodial parent.
The direction was issued by Justice Lalitha Kanneganti while hearing a custody dispute involving a nine-year-old boy. The judge in her Sept 29 order observed, "a child should not be made to view his or her relationship with a parent through the term 'visitation,' which carries an unfortunate suggestion that one parent is a part of the child's life, while the other merely comes to visit."
The case before the high court was of a father, who lives in Noida but works in Chennai, and had not seen his son for nine years.
Despite this, the trial court had granted him 50% custody during the child’s vacations, apart from regular weekend access. The court questioned whether such an arrangement could be imposed without first assessing the family’s circumstances, hearing the child’s views and determining whether the proposed arrangement was practical and in the child’s best interests.
The mother, who lives in Bengaluru, had approached HC challenging an Aug 7, 2026, order passed by a court in Bengaluru Rural which had granted the father access to the child every Saturday and Sunday for three to four hours between 11am and 7pm, until disposal of the petition.
The father was also permitted to communicate through WhatsApp or any other device for about 30 minutes between 7.30pm and 8.30pm on alternate days, subject to prior intimation to the mother. The HC stayed the order while examining the circumstances surrounding the custody arrangement.
“Calling it parenting time recognises a simple truth that no parent is a visitor in the life of a child,” Justice Kanneganti observed.

stories.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar cautions Ministers against possible ‘sting operations’
stories.deck: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar is learnt to have warned his Cabinet colleagues to remain vigilant against possible sting operations, amid reports that private agencies could be secretly recording Ministers’ conversations, meetings, and movements
stories.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar is learnt to have warned his Cabinet colleagues to remain vigilant against possible sting operations, amid reports that private agencies could be secretly recording Ministers’ conversations, meetings, and movements.
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara and Minister H.C. Balakrishna, who attended the Cabinet meeting on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), confirmed that Mr. Shivakumar, who also holds the Intelligence portfolio, had alerted the Ministers about possible sting operations.
“Since the Chief Minister holds the Intelligence portfolio, he cautioned us based on some information he had received,” Mr. Parameshwara told reporters.
Mr. Shivakumar is learnt to have raised the issue at the Cabinet meeting and shown the Ministers a “file” containing details of alleged ongoing sting operations. The file reportedly included the names of a few Ministers who were purportedly being targeted.
The Chief Minister is said to have advised the Ministers to exercise caution in the light of these purported developments. The Ministers were also reportedly advised to be cautious about meeting strangers privately or allowing themselves to be photographed with unfamiliar persons.
Political charge
Mr. Balakrishna, meanwhile, sought to link the alleged sting operations to Janata Dal (Secular) leader H.D. Kumaraswamy, accusing him of attempting to damage the Chief Minister’s political standing.
“Why did he not remember the NICE land issue and undertake a padayatra when Siddaramaiah was Chief Minister?” Mr. Balakrishna asked, referring to Mr. Kumaraswamy’s recent political campaigns against the Congress government.
The Minister alleged that Mr. Kumaraswamy had been using protests and padayatras since Mr. Shivakumar became Chief Minister in an attempt to undermine his position as a prominent Vokkaliga leader.
His remarks also referred to the State’s long history of political allegations involving purported CDs, pen drives and other forms of recorded material. About a decade ago, Mr. Kumaraswamy had claimed that he possessed CDs containing material relating to alleged corruption involving former Minister G. Janardhana Reddy, though the material was not subsequently made public.
The latest warning comes at a time when political activity is intensifying in Karnataka, with the major parties already positioning themselves for the 2028 Assembly elections.
This is not the first time Mr. Shivakumar has cautioned Congress leaders about possible action against them by investigating agencies. During the Enforcement Directorate searches involving the family members of Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi, he had claimed Congress MLAs and Ministers were under the agency’s scanner and urged party leaders to remain cautious.
The latest claims about alleged sting operations, however, have not been independently established.
Long history
The latest episode also revives Karnataka’s long history of political battles involving recorded conversations and purportedly incriminating material — from audio tapes in the 1980s to video CDs, sting operations, pen drives and, more recently, digitally recorded conversations and videos.
Such material has periodically been used as a political weapon, with allegations, counter-allegations, and demands for investigations often becoming part of electoral and intra-party battles.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court orders using ‘parenting time’ instead of ‘visitation’ in all child custody cases
stories.deck: “Calling it ‘parenting time’ recognises a simple truth that no parent is a ‘visitor’ in the life of a child”
stories.bodyText:
In a significant move aimed at reforming the language used in cases involving custody of a child between couples in conflict, the High Court of Karnataka has directed all family courts and courts dealing with guardians and wards (G&WC) cases henceforth to use the term “parenting time” instead of “visitation,” observing that no parent should be treated as a mere “visitor” in a child’s life.
Justice Lalitha Kanneganti, who was hearing a child custody case, issued the direction while pointing out that it is time for a small change in the language employed in judicial proceedings.
Pointing out that courts often use the word “visitation” to describe the time the child spends with a parent, who is a non-custodial parent, the court said that the word “visitation” is familiar, but “it carries an unfortunate suggestion that one parent is part of the child’s life while the other merely visits.”
“A child should not be made to understand the relationship through the word visitation, which is used for someone who arrives and leaves as a guest. Children read the conduct of adults and sometimes the words of courts to understand where they belong. Calling it parenting time recognises a simple truth that no parent is a visitor in the life of a child,” the court said.
Though a change in terminology does not decide questions of custody, when a court imposes restrictions on the access to the child, the word “parenting” is more humane, Justice Kanneganti said.
Also, the High Court directed the Registrar of General to issue a circular to all courts in this regard on the use of “parenting time” while also directing that even in the applications for child’s custody the word “parenting time” should be used instead of “visitation.”

stories.headline: Tourism dept pushes ahead with court-permitted works in Roerich Estate in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Amid judicial scrutiny of the development of the scenic Roerich–Devika Rani Estate, off Kanakapura Road in south Bengaluru, tourism department has stepped up efforts to fast-track works permitted by high court.
The department’s efforts have left conservationists worried about the possible impact of tourism-related interventions on the sensitive landscape, which is part of a deemed forest and located adjacent to an elephant corridor.
Reviewing the eco-tourism project’s progress at the estate, tourism minister KJ George inspected the site along with officials from tourism and forest departments, and Jungle Lodges and Resorts (JLR). The minister directed officials to ensure the property’s ecological, cultural and artistic character is preserved, complete permitted works within the stipulated timeline, while ensuring visitor amenities are created without compromising the estate’s natural landscape.
Stating that the eco-tourism project is based on a balanced model, tourism secretary Ram Prasath Manohar said, “The department is creating a balanced model where conservation remains central to the project, while essential visitor facilities are developed sensitively, keeping in mind the ecological importance of the landscape. 
Subsequent works, other than those approved by the court, will be taken up in consultation with the departments concerned.”
Conservationists who have been pursuing the matter before high court have argued that govt has violated provisions of Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, by not obtaining prior permission or clearance to undertake work, as the landscape is part of a deemed forest. However, forest officials clarified that such clearance is mandatory only for non-forestry activities and that the eco-tourism project constitutes forestry activity.
“Even though the landscape is deemed forest, ownership rests with the estate owners (govt). Tourism department is free to take up any forestry-related work on the property. Only if the department wants to take up development works outside the estate premises will it need to obtain clearance. As of now, the department has not violated any norms,” explained an official who was part of the inspection.

Bengaluru
: An AI-based survey of 2,493.5km of roads across Bengaluru North City Corporation’s seven divisions and 72 wards has identified 14,393 potholes, with 82.1% of the surveyed roads classified as being in good-to-adequate condition.
The survey, conducted using real-time images captured through dashcams, found 1,426.8km of roads in good condition and another 607.1km with minor surface defects. The remaining included localised road damage, utility-related damage and unpaved roads.
Byatarayanapura division recorded the highest number of potholes at 5,964, followed by Sarvagnanagar with 2,359 and Pulikeshi Nagar (1,357). The survey also identified 102km of roads affected by utility works and 102.8km of unpaved roads.
The corporation said data will be used to prioritise road repairs and development, shifting road maintenance from a complaint-based approach to data- and technology-based planning.

briefs.headline: Drought-hit Karnataka bets on ₹3.8 cr Azolla mission to protect dairy farmers
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 With 
drought
 threatening to shrink fodder availability and push up cattle-rearing costs, govt has launched a Rs 3.8-crore mission to establish 12,000 azolla production units across all 240 taluks in the state.
The animal husbandry and veterinary services department initiative comes amid dwindling fodder reserves and strained supplies from neighbouring states. Stock of fodder in at least 22 taluks is sufficient for less than 20 weeks, raising concerns over livestock nutrition if drought persists.
Azolla, a fast-growing aquatic fern rich in protein, minerals and other nutrients, is being promoted as a low-cost supplementary feed, especially for milk-yielding cattle. The crop can be cultivated in compact units near cattle sheds or homes with access to clean water.
Each unit is estimated to cost Rs 3,150 and requires a space of about 10ft x 4ft x 1ft. The setup includes UV-stabilised HDPE sheets, shade nets, supporting frames, soil, cow dung, super phosphate, starter culture and labour.
“The idea is to help small and marginal livestock farmers produce a nutritious supplementary feed without depending on conventional fodder supplies,” an official said. 
“Farmers need not invest anything as the govt will foot input costs. Interested farmers will be trained in Azolla farming, harvesting and processing.”
The units will be rolled out through gram panchayats, with priority given to livestock farmers who have adequate space and access to clean water. “Each unit will be geo-tagged, with beneficiary details and photographs recorded to ensure proper implementation under the VB-G RAM G framework and Gram Panchayat Development Plan for greater accountability,” the official said.
Officials say the current situation is more challenging than previous droughts, when 
Karnataka
 could rely on maize stalk and paddy straw from neighbouring states.
“We used to import these from Tamil Nadu and Telangana but with much of peninsular India reeling under drought, traditional supply lines offer little reassurance,” G Parameshwara, deputy CM and revenue minister, told the assembly during the special session on drought.
Although the animal husbandry department estimates that the state has enough fodder stock for an average of 30 to 40 weeks, shortages in individual taluks are worrying.
“The govt has also released Rs 25 crore to buy and distribute fodder seed kits to encourage farmers to grow their own feed if they have irrigation facilities,” Parameshwara said. “Besides, Karnataka Milk Federation is also supporting fodder seed distribution and promoting fodder cultivation among dairy farmers.” Gram panchayats have also been directed to undertake fodder cultivation works under VB-G RAM G scheme.
Govt is also exploring the use of fertile lake beds for fodder cultivation. Rural development and panchayat raj minister Eshwar Khandre has directed zilla panchayat CEOs to identify suitable lake beds for the purpose.
“Even when lakes are full, swathes of their beds remain exposed,” Khandre said. “This land is fertile and retains soil moisture, making them ideal for fodder cultivation. The jurisdictional gram panchayats will oversee cultivation under the VB-G RAM G scheme. We will launch a pilot project in a few days in Bidar.”

briefs.headline: East Bengaluru lake volunteers seek patrolling, action against littering
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Residents and volunteers who have been cleaning and maintaining lakes in east Bengaluru say their efforts are being undone by inadequate security and lack of sustained action by authorities.
Residents of Nallurhalli and Pattandur Agrahara near Whitefield said the challenge is not merely cleaning lakes, but also preventing littering and unauthorised activities. At Nallurhalli Lake, residents said Ganesha idols were immersed by unauthorised persons. After authorities failed to act on complaints, volunteers removed the idols themselves.
“There is no proper patrolling. The plan is to deploy six home guards to guard the lake, but it has not yet been finalised,” said Shyam Padhi, a citizen volunteer working on waste management and lake-related issues around Whitefield.
Padhi said he conducted a cleanup drive at Nallurhalli Lake about two weeks ago, but garbage had already accumulated again. Residents alleged that bulk waste handling agencies segregate waste on the roadside near the lake and that some garbage is left uncollected and burnt during the early hours.
A portion of the lake’s fencing has been damaged, residents said, allowing people to enter and litter or defecate. They said the lake had become a hangout for drinkers after dusk. 
Empty beer bottles and cartons have been found inside the lake compound.
Residents also raised concerns over ITPL Back Lake, where greywater from surrounding slums and residences is entering the waterbody. “The lake has become filthy and a health hazard; a breeding ground for mosquitoes. Around 2,000 apartments around the lake are affected,” Padhi said.
Residents said officials had told them the lake was undeveloped and funds were yet to be cleared for fencing, park development and maintenance. Following several complaints over recent weeks, Bengaluru East City Corporation officials inspected ITPL Back Lake Tuesday and imposed fines on some individuals for littering.
BECC additional commissioner Snehal Lokhande said Ganesha idols will be cleared soon, adding that officials were attending to the issue across multiple lakes in BECC limits.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru traffic claims life: Man dies of heart attack on flyover next to hospital
briefs.deck: On a Monday night, KK Sajir experienced a heart attack while stuck in heavy traffic on Hosur Road. His friends rushed to get him to a nearby hospital directly beneath the flyover, but they found themselves trapped for almost 35 minutes in gridlock. Sadly, by the time Sajir reached the hospital, he was pronounced dead. The traffic congestion has been largely attributed to ongoing construction in…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: For 51-year-old KK Sajir, a heart attack turned into a desperate race against time. But on a stretch of road notorious for traffic snarls, there was nowhere for his friends to go.
Around 11 pm Monday, Sajir was travelling in a Bolero pickup with his friend Najaf towards Hosur to meet another friend. As they approached Chandapura on NH-44, they took the flyover. Minutes later, Sajir complained of severe chest pain. The pain soon became unbearable, and he told Najaf he could no longer drive.
Najaf did not know how to drive. He began desperately seeking help, but vehicles quickly piled up behind them, leaving the Bolero trapped in the traffic jam on the flyover. Traffic barely moved. What made the situation even more agonising was that a hospital stood directly below the flyover.
“There was a hospital right below the flyover. But they were stuck on top of it. They simply could not get down,” said Saleem Malik, a friend of Sajir and Najaf and a member of the All Kerala Muslim Cultural Centre.
Najaf frantically waved at motorists behind them, pleading for help, and called the emergency number 108. 
But the congestion on Hosur Road left him with little room to manoeuvre.
“He kept telling people to help him. He could see the hospital below but could not reach it. Nobody could do anything in the bumper-to-bumper traffic for nearly 35 minutes,” said Malik, who reached the spot in an autorickshaw after being alerted by Najaf. In fact, it took Malik nearly 55 minutes to reach Sajir’s Bolero because of the traffic jam. By the time Sajir was moved into an autorickshaw and taken to the hospital, it was too late. Doctors declared him dead.
For Sajir, the distance to emergency care was less but the traffic jam on the flyover became an insurmountable barrier. The tragedy has once again exposed the deadly consequences of Bengaluru’s notorious traffic congestion, particularly along the heavily crowded Hosur Road corridor.
A former supermarket owner and native of Kannur in Kerala, Sajir had come to Bengaluru in search of a job. He is survived by his wife Rahina and six children. His last rites were conducted in his hometown on Tuesday. “The traffic was so bad, it just took my friend away forever,” Malik lamented.
What is causing jam on Hosur Road?
NHAI has attributed a significant part of the recent congestion to the railway overbridge (ROB) being constructed by K-RIDE as part of the Byappanahalli-Hosur railway doubling project
With traffic snarls worsening on the Hosur Road stretch near Chandapura, agencies involved in ongoing infrastructure works have begun trading blame over what is causing the congestion.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has attributed a significant part of the recent congestion to the railway overbridge (ROB) being constructed by K-RIDE as part of the Byappanahalli-Hosur railway doubling project. K-RIDE, however, has rejected the claim, saying its temporary structures have not encroached upon the carriageway.
According to NHAI, construction work for the road infrastructure near the railway bridge can be taken up only after K-RIDE completes its work at the location. K-RIDE managing director Lakshman Singh said the railway construction was not responsible for the traffic congestion. He said the temporary structures had been placed in the median and outside the road boundary and therefore did not obstruct traffic.
“The width of the National Highway is inconsistent and the temporary structures do not affect traffic. They are placed in the median and outside the road boundaries,” Singh said. The local police, however, have a different assessment. Surya Nagar police said the ongoing railway construction was contributing significantly to the congestion and that they had temporarily asked the agency to halt work following the recent rains.

briefs.headline: Southwest monsoon rainfall in Karnataka is second lowest in 70 years and seventh lowest in 125 years
briefs.deck: The year 2002, which had the lowest southwest monsoon rainfall since 1956, had received just 10 mm less than 2026
briefs.bodyText:
The rainfall received by Karnataka during the southwest monsoon (SWM) is the second lowest in the last 70 years (after 1956) and the seventh lowest in the last 125 years (after 1901), shows data, pointing to the severity of the drought. The year 2002, which had the lowest SWM rainfall since 1956, had received just 10 mm less than 2026.
As against the normal rainfall of 852 mm for the SWM period from June to September, the State received only 551 mm, reporting a shortage of 35%.
What has caused concern is that while the overall rainfall deficit is 35%, the actual shortage is even higher in some regions. The cumulative rainfall deficit during the southwest monsoon stands at 41% for South Interior Karnataka, 42% for North Interior Karnataka, 38% for Malnad region, and 28% for coastal region. SWM has been either deficit or largely deficit in 209 taluks of the total 240 in the State.
The State has already declared 217 taluks as drought hit as per the Centre’s drought manual’s norms. This number is likely to increase as the ground-truthing exercise is on in the remaining 23 taluks.
Repeated droughts
Drought is not a new phenomenon for Karnataka, which stands next only to Rajasthan in terms of drought-prone areas, as 80% of its geographical area is prone to drought. Since 2001, the State has faced drought for 16 years. But the present drought stands out for its severity and impact on lives of people, particularly agriculture sector.
Unlike a few other States, including Tamil Nadu, that can rely on the northeast monsoon (NEM), Karnataka depends prominently on SWM, which is the mainstay of the State’s weather system, accounting for about 74% of the calendar year rainfall. NEM accounts for a just 16%. This means that the impact of the drought is bound to grow when the shortage of water is expected to increase.
Already, the agriculture sector has taken a serious hit during the kharif season. While the sowing coverage for the season, which marks the main agricultural season for the State, took a hit owing to poor rains, most of those who took up sowing had to face losses since crops wilted because of prolonged dry spells.
Huge crop losses
As against the target of 84.1 lakh hectares, sowing was undertaken only on 69.57 lakh hectares in the State during kharif, accounting for a coverage of 83%. Foodgrains in general and cereals in particular are the crops that saw lesser coverage in terms of sowing. As against a target of 37.6 lakh hectares, cereals were sown only on 27.27 lakh hectares, accounting for 73% coverage. The total coverage of foodgrains accounted for 76% as they were sown on 46.21 lakh hectares as against a target of 60.45 lakh hectares.
Worse, a sizeable extent of crops that were sown dried up. The assessment in 101 taluks alone has shown that standing crops on a total of 19.52 lakh hectares worth around ₹18,748.23 crore have been lost. The total crop losses in 201 taluks has been estimated to be around ₹46,000 crore. These figures are likely to increase when crop losses in other taluks are also considered.
While the State has already submitted two memoranda to the Centre seeking assistance to overcome the crisis, agricultural experts and policy makers fear that the food production may take a severe hit this year.

briefs.headline: Five injured in separate electrical infrastructure blasts in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Bescom officials said that they will bear the medical expenses of the injured person in this case.
briefs.bodyText:
Five people were injured in two separate incidents — one involving the bursting of a transformer at Benniganahalli and another a ring main unit (RMU) on Bagalur Road — in Bengaluru, officials said.
The first incident occurred around 12.30 pm on October 6 near the Coca Cola godown at Benniganahalli, within the limits of Ramamurthy Nagar police station.
Four persons — Narayana, 50, Azeem Pasha, Chethan, 23, and Lakshmi, 22 — sustained injuries in the incident. The injured persons, who are from different parts of Bengaluru, are undergoing treatment in a hospital, police said. A motorcycle was also damaged.
Ramamurthy Nagar police have launched an investigation into the incident.
A Bescom official said, “We have visited the injured persons. We will bear all expenses for their medical treatment.”
The second incident occurred around 9.30 a.m. on October 7 near Bagaluru Cross. An RMU reportedly burst, injuring Mohammed Afroz, who was walking on the footpath. He was taken to a hospital for treatment.
A video of the incident shows Afroz walking on the footpath near the electrical equipment when it suddenly bursts.
Bescom officials said an RMU is part of a medium-voltage power distribution network, and that such bursting incidents are rare. Technical officials said that they are monitoring the situation on the ground.
“Our preliminary investigation suggested that the incident occurred due to a 3-way RMU CT flashover, which resulted in a blast. A pedestrian walking nearby was injured. A 3-way RMU CT flashover means an electrical arc or flashover occurring around the current transformer inside the RMU,” an official said.
Bescom officials said that they will bear the medical expenses of the injured person in this case.
The Yelahanka police are investigating the Bagaluru Cross incident.

stories.headline: US mortgage rates jump to 7.49%, hit highest level in nearly 3 years
stories.deck: In a notable shift, US mortgage rates have climbed to an alarming 7.49 percent, the peak since November 2023. This increase has further strained the housing market as the election period looms. Mortgage applications saw a 4.2 percent decline last week, reaching their lowest point since February 2025, highlighting ongoing affordability challenges for potential buyers and resulting in fewer…
stories.bodyText:
US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years, with the sharp rise in borrowing costs adding to pressure on the housing market as Americans head towards November 3 elections.
The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) said, as cited by Reuters. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.
Mortgage applications dropped 4.2% last week from the previous week, while refinancing applications fell sharply. Overall application volumes are now at their lowest since February 2025 and have declined nearly 50% since January.
"Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist told Reuters.
Mortgage rates have closely followed movements in the yield on 10-year US treasury notes. Earlier this week, the yield topped 5.3%, reaching a 24-year high, with concerns over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth driving the rise.
Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar increase in the 10-year treasury yield.
The increase comes at a politically sensitive time, with the US mid-term elections just four weeks away. The cost of living was the top issue among Americans in deciding how they would vote, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday. At the same time, US President Donald Trump's approval rating stood at a record low of 32%.
Inflation has also risen, reaching 3.4% in August on a measure targeted by the Federal Reserve at 2%.
Fed policymakers have signalled that they expect another interest-rate increase by the end of the year following the rate hike in September. Markets are currently betting that policymakers will not raise rates at the next meeting at the end of October.
The latest increase in mortgage rates comes as affordability remains under pressure for buyers, while the decline in loan applications points to weaker activity in the mortgage market.

stories.headline: Elon Musk alleges ‘oligarch’ interference in Starlink’s India launch
stories.deck: Mr. Musk made the allegation hours after Lauren Dreyer, a SpaceX executive, said she hoped that the service would be operational in India by next year
stories.bodyText:
Years into SpaceX’s efforts to get permissions to operate its satellite broadband service in India, the firm’s founder and CEO Elon Musk has accused “certain oligarchs” in India of stimieying the service’s launch in India. Mr. Musk made the accusation on X, formerly Twitter, hours after one of his firm’s executives said she hoped that the service would be live in India by 2027.
Responding to a user on X who was demanding the launch of Starlink in India, Mr. Musk said, “Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are …This is a crime against the people of India!”
While Starlink has obtained a Global Mobile Personal Communications by Satellite (GMPCS) authorisation from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), the government has not yet cleared security approvals that Starlink needs to operate. These requirements, some of which were amended last May, require SpaceX to disable Starlink receivers purchased outside India, and to also disable terminals sold in India abroad. This is on top of extensive surveillance requirements that apply across the telecom and broadband sector.
Furthermore, telecom operators have stiffly resisted the so-called “administrative assignment” of satellite spectrum, which would entail allowing Starlink and other operators to use airwaves for a fixed fee, instead of having to participate in an auction. Since satellite spectrum is usually shared without issue in most countries, Reliance Jio has argued that the 2012 2G spectrum judgement of the Supreme Court prohibits such an assignment. The firm has sent legal opinions to the Union government, including one in 2024 by retired Supreme Court justice L. Nageshwar Rao.
“We can’t talk about building the future at scale without talking about closing the digital divide, because otherwise we’d just be building a future that leaves a substantial portion of the population behind,” Lauren Dreyer, Vice President of Starlink Business Operations at SpaceX said at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) on Tuesday.

stories.headline: As GST Council meets, tax experts say reforms must move beyond rates to processes and compliance
stories.deck: The GST Council will meet in New Delhi on October 8 for the first time after its meeting on September 3-4, 2025.
stories.bodyText:
With the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system having settled down, revenues remaining steady, and rates having been rationalised, tax experts across the board say the priority for the GST Council in its 57th meeting on October 8 should be on decisively easing the compliance burden for taxpayers.
The GST Council will meet in New Delhi on October 8 for the first time after its meeting on September 3-4, 2025, when it had introduced wide-ranging rate and slab changes. Sources in the Ministry of Finance have confirmed that the meeting will not deliberate on GST rates and will instead focus on a five-pronged effort to reform the tax system and its administration.
Tax analysts agree that this should be the priority of the Council.
Right time for reforms
The GST system turned nine years old on July 1, 2026. Through this time, the Council has met 56 times, has reformed the GST slabs, successfully implemented the 5-year compensation period to States, and the system has stabilised in terms of revenue.
“With high GST collections across the past few months, the GST Council in its next meeting scheduled on October 8, would be able to decide on several issues faced by businesses including relaxation of input tax credit restrictions, reducing complaints for service providers, providing faster refunds, etc, without being unduly worried about the impact of such measures on the GST collections,” MS Mani, Partner at Deloitte India, said.
The Hindu had reported on October 6 that the proposals by the Centre for the GST Council’s consideration would cover process reforms, structural reforms, ease of living and doing business, exports of services, and e-commerce. The final decisions will, however, be made clear only once the Council’s meeting concludes.
Several areas for improvement
“The most important process reforms will be allowing automatic and easy refunds especially to exporters, and preventing ITC accumulation, because these are economy wide effects on working capital for firms,” Rahul Ahluwalia, Founder Director of the Foundation for Economic Development said.
Prabhat Ranjan, Senior Director at Nexdigm, a business and tax consultancy, said that while rate rationalisation remains important, certainty of tax treatment can be as important as the rates themselves.
“A significant hidden cost of GST arises from interpretational uncertainty — whether on classification, input tax credit, valuation, place of supply or procedural requirements,” Mr. Ranjan explained. “When the same transaction can invite different positions across jurisdictions, businesses face not merely additional tax exposure but litigation costs, provisioning requirements, working-capital blockage and uncertainty in commercial decision-making.”
Technology to the rescue
Brijesh Agrawal, CEO of Busy Infotech, a company specialising in GST-related software services, said that the GST back-end system has become technologically sophisticated but everyday compliance remains complex for business owners.
“Key priorities should centre on consolidating tax slabs to a maximum of three [currently there are 6 slabs, including Zero/Nil, 0.25% and 3%], eliminating cess and overhauling Section 17(5) to allow unconditional credit on all verifiable business-to-business expenses,” Mr. Agrawal said.
At the moment, ordinary business costs are not entitled to input tax credits and so not only add to the costs of doing business but also potentially add to the price of the final product being sold.
The Hindu has learnt that the Centre is proposing a change in this regard, to allow ordinary business costs to also be included in the ambit of input tax credits.
Single registrations and audit
Another proposal that will be put up before the GST Council is to allow businesses to register in a single State and sell across the country instead of having to register their business in each of the States they want to sell in.
Nitin Vijaivergia, Partner, Price Waterhouse & Co further said that the proposed system of harmonising GST audits across multiple registrations would significantly ease the compliance burden on large taxpayers.
“A unified approach to issues that cuts across State lines would curb duplicative information requests and eliminate the risk of divergent conclusions on the same transaction,” Mr. Vijaivergia said.
“It would also equip tax authorities to deploy data analytics and risk parameters with precision, directing scrutiny where genuine risk lies,” he added. “For businesses, the dividend is clear: greater consistency, enhanced predictability and a leaner audit-related compliance cost.”

briefs.headline: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist
briefs.deck: As tensions escalate in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices have surged amid fears of potential supply disruptions. Recent assaults on tankers heighten the danger of transporting crude through this vital corridor. Additionally, American crude inventories are dwindling, signaling a tighter market, while diesel and jet fuel stocks remain below average levels, a…
briefs.bodyText:
Oil prices inched higher on Thursday as concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%, while WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or 1.13%.
The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session, when the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up the release of oil stocks and give priority to diesel supplies. The plan, launched in March, is aimed at dealing with record fuel prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.
Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has become a growing concern as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month. Before the war, the route handled shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies.
The pressure on shipping has increased even as Gulf producers raise exports. Tanker attacks through the Strait reached their highest level last week for any week since the Iran war began, leaving crude shipments facing higher costs and greater risks for cargoes and crew.
A tanker north of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles in the latest attack, causing casualties, the United Kingdom maritime trade operations agency said on Wednesday.
Supply concerns were accompanied by signs of tighter US inventories. According to Reuters, American crude stocks fell by 3.2 million barrels in the week ended October 2 to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration. The decline was larger than the 1.7 million-barrel fall analysts had expected in a Reuters poll.
Diesel and jet fuel inventories also declined, with distillate fuel stocks falling by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels. Those inventories remained below their levels for this period of the year over the past five years.
Oil markets have remained unsettled for more than seven months since the Middle East conflict began. Even with the latest increase, prices are still below the $126 a barrel level reached earlier in the crisis.

This change means that postpaid plans will now begin at Rs 499, reflecting increased costs for consumers. Other telecom operators are expected to follow Airtel’s lead in adjusting their…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Be prepared to shell out higher mobile tariffs. Bharti Airtel will from Thursday hike postpaid tariffs by 3- 10%. India’s second-largest telecom operator has included free international roaming (for one trip per SIM) worth Rs 2,000 in all postpaid plans, which will go up by Rs 50. The new postpaid plan rental plans will now start at Rs 499. Other operators may follow suit.
In past few months, telecom service providers have been encouraging users to move to higher-value plans to improve their average revenue per user (ARPU) by adding new services and discontinuing their lower charge plans. Earlier this year, Vodafone Idea had also hiked prices for some of its postpaid family packs by 7-9%.
According to Centrum Institutional Research, the pricing environment in the telecom industry has become more favourable and a tariff hike of 12-15% over the next four-to-five months could be on the cards.

MUMBAI: Brookfield is making its foray into the local industrial and logistics real estate market with a $450 million (Rs 4,300 crore) purchase of eight warehousing parks from ESR India, expanding its footprint beyond the country's office and hospitality spaces. Capital will also be deployed towards future development of the portfolio, Brookfield said in a statement on Wednesday.
Spread across nearly 400 acres, the portfolio covers major cities including Mumbai, Pune, Delhi-NCR, Chennai and Kolkata, providing access to key consumption centres and logistics catchments. About 98% of the space is leased, catering to a diversified mix of logistics and industrial occupiers.
ESR will continue to manage the properties in the near term. Leasing volumes in India's industrial and warehousing space reached 36.8 million sq ft in H1 2026, a 15% increase over the same period last year, Knight Frank said in a report published earlier this year.
The demand is led by manufacturing and third-party logistics occupiers, analysts at the firm said, adding that the completion of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor in March boosted the growth of the market. In Nov last year, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB) and local warehouse developer IndoSpace acquired six industrial and logistics parks in a deal worth over $300 million through their joint venture.

briefs.headline: Consolidated account statements to reflect deposits in banks
briefs.deck: Individuals will soon benefit from easier access to financial assets in one place through RBI's measures. Interoperable account aggregators will enable customers to access financial information across various banks with consent. Survivors of deceased account holders will find it simpler to discover unclaimed deposits. Additionally, bank deposit information will be included in the monthly…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Individuals may soon find it easier to see their financial assets in one place. 
RBI
 on Wednesday announced two measures: making account aggregators interoperable and allowing bank-deposit information to be added to the monthly consolidated account statement (CAS), which currently captures holdings such as shares, mutual funds and pensions. The move will make it easier for survivors of deceased account holders to discover their financial assets and reduce the number of unclaimed deposits.
Interoperability will allow customers to use any account aggregator to access and share financial information held across different banks and other financial-information providers. With about 15 account aggregators, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said information was fragmented; linking them would make it easier for individuals, insurers, asset managers and investment advisers to use it, with the customer's consent.
Account aggregators let customers securely consolidate and share financial data from multiple banks and financial institutions with their consent. For lenders, this provides a faster view of income, cash flows and liabilities for credit assessment; for personal-finance apps, it brings fragmented financial information into one dashboard.
RBI is also facilitating the inclusion of bank deposits in CAS through account aggregators. Demat holders will thus be able to see securities and bank deposits together, while those without demat accounts will continue to obtain and share a consolidated view of their financial information through account aggregators.

briefs.headline: At 107, National Company Law Tribunal OKs record insolvency cases
briefs.deck: The National Company Law Tribunal approved 107 corporate insolvency cases in the last quarter of the fiscal year. These cases had an estimated value of Rs 11,000 crore compared to previous quarters. However, the tribunal now faces significant vacancies among its members and challenges in its operations. With many judges retiring soon, the functioning of the tribunal is further affected.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved a record 107 corporate insolvency cases during the last quarter, but stares at the prospect of a moderation in the pace due to a large number of vacancies.
Data released by NCLT estimated the value of cases approved at Rs 11,000 crore during the Sept quarter, as against Rs 5,500 crore involved in the June quarter when 78 cases were approved. During Oct-Dec 2025, the tribunal had approved 90 cases, the previous high. Since April 2017, it has cleared 1,735 cases with 185 approved so far this fiscal, as against 257 during 2025-26.
During the last quarter, the Mumbai bench approved 35 resolution plans, followed by 29 by the principal bench and the New Delhi bench.
At the end of Sept, there were 335 pending cases across its 12 benches, as against 363 in April-end. Of the pending cases, orders have been reserved in 41 cases, with the Supreme Court, high courts and NCLAT ordering a stay in 24.
With no member appointed since the start of 2025, barring the president Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, NCLT is 14 members short of the sanctioned strength of 62, with four more retiring by Dec.
"As a result, 13 courts are functioning on a full-day basis and 18 on a half-day basis," said NCLT.
It is also facing another challenge -- the ratio between judicial and administrative strength. Judicial members currently outnumber technical members 26 to 22, making it difficult to constitute benches as each bench requires representation from both categories. While govt has initiated the process of selecting new members, the exercise is time-consuming and members also have to undergo training after they join.
The tribunal is urging members to clear cases at a faster pace with the president also monitoring the performance of the benches across the country.

briefs.headline: Premium spirits sales soar past cheaper liquor: Report
briefs.deck: Premium spirits in India are experiencing significant growth with a rise in sales volumes projected until 2025. Cheaper liquor categories show slower growth, which indicates a changing market composition. Indian malt whiskies are among the fastest-growing segments, surpassing Scotch malts in sales volume in 2024. The overall spirits market is expected to expand steadily, driven by rising incomes…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Premium spirits are growing several times faster than cheaper liquor in India, with higher-priced products gaining a larger share of sales, according to a report by industry body International Spirits and Wines Association of India (ISWAI).
Sales volumes in the premium segment grew at a compound annual rate of 10.2% between 2022 and 2025. That compares with 1.1% for the report's lowest-priced category and 1.4% for regular spirits. Overall spirits volumes grew 3.7% annually over the same period. Super-premium Indian-made spirits grew even faster, at about 34% annually. However, this segment remains small, accounting for less than 1% of total spirits volumes in the report's 2025 estimates.
Cheaper products continue to account for a substantial part of the market. The lowest-priced and regular categories together made up nearly half of spirits sales volumes in 2025. Their slower growth nevertheless points to a change in the mix of products being sold.
"Rising incomes, evolving consumer aspirations, and greater availability of premium products are reshaping the market mix," the report said.
It also linked the shift to changes in liquor retailing. Stores offering wider selections, better product displays and space for customers to browse are encouraging shoppers to explore brands and spend more, according to the report.
Indian malt whiskies were among the faster-growing categories. Their volumes expanded at about 39% annually between 2022 and 2025, compared with about 5% for Scotch malts, the report estimated. It said Indian malts overtook Scotch malts in sales volumes in 2024.
Imported spirits also grew faster than the broader spirits market, although their share remained modest. Their volumes rose about 8% annually over the three years, taking their market share from 2.4% to 2.7%. ISWAI estimated India's alcoholic beverages market at about Rs 6.2 lakh crore ($71 billion).

briefs.headline: Survey: 12% in India report being scammed in last 1 year
briefs.deck: According to a recent GSMA survey, 12% of respondents in India reported being scammed recently. Online shopping scams are the most prevalent type among Indian consumers compared to other scams. The survey indicates that messaging apps are frequently used by scammers targeting Indian victims. GSMA highlights the increasing challenge of digital fraud on a global scale. Telecommunications operators…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A survey conducted by GSMA, a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, has found 12% of respondents in India reported being scammed in the last 12 months as opposed to 8% in Asean-6 - Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam and Philippines.
"Indian consumers also extend institutions an unusual level of permission to use their data," said the India Consumer Scam Report 2026.
"Online shopping scams, at 33%, are the most common type in India compared with 32% across Asean-6, followed by prize, lottery and inheritance scams at 31%, compared with 25% (Asean-6), and job or income scams at 30%, compared with 32%. Scams using a QR code or payment link stand at 27% in India, compared to 18% across Asean-6 and 23% in Thailand. Messaging apps are the most common route, involved in 42% of Indian victims' scams against 41% across Asean-6," said the report.
GSMA chief regulatory officer John Giusti told TOI that the challenge of digital economy frauds is growing globally and telecom operators in India, along with authorities here, are at the "forefront" of tackling the menace. "One trillion dollars were lost to scams worldwide in 2024 and 50% of consumers (globally) have said they're being exposed to scams.
"India led the way in 5G rollout globally and has a significant headstart in 6G too. Telecom operators here are leading the way in tackling the menace. Your phone just flashed a likely spam and that shows the attempt being made to safeguard consumers," said Giusti.
"Whether it be scam calls, scam advertisements on digital platforms, scammers are trying to find ways to infiltrate financial services. Globally everyone needs to come together and solve this problem," he said.
GSMA has used these findings on a cross-sectional online survey of adults in India and the six Asean markets through self-administered online interviews between July 29, 2026 and Aug 3 with about 500 respondents in India.

briefs.headline: Property taxation needs structural reform
briefs.deck: The property tax performance of India’s municipal bodies has been poor — India’s cumulative property tax was 0.15-0.2% of its GDP
briefs.bodyText:
A robust property tax system is vital for India’s cities. Property tax is not just the most important own revenue source for India’s municipal bodies, it is also critical to bridge the gap in urban investment, as such investment depends on municipal creditworthiness. However, the property tax performance of India’s municipal bodies has been poor — India’s cumulative property tax was 0.15-0.2% of its GDP, whereas it was 0.6% in middle-income countries and 0.3% in low-income countries. Policy efforts have sought to improve the property tax performance of India’s municipal bodies through technology and process-based reforms recommended by successive Finance Commissions and national schemes such as the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission and the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation. Yet, tax outcomes remain sub-optimal. Why?
Two recent studies offer insights — a working paper on Chennai’s property tax by Nobel Laureate Esther Duflo and co-authors, and this writer’s research on Bengaluru, Pune and Ghaziabad’s property tax. Both studies found that technology and process-based reforms will keep yielding sub-optimal results unless backed by structural reforms. Firstly, Duflo and co-authors’ research in Chennai found that municipal human resources are a critical determinant of property tax outcomes. It also finds that a municipality’s own tax assessors achieve far better tax outcomes compared to assessors from outsourced firms. The research conducted across Bengaluru, Pune and Ghaziabad finds that in addition to the issue of municipal human resource deficits, two other structural issues — irregularity in the conduct of elections and poor financial reporting practices — also impact tax outcomes.
Stages of property tax
There are three life stages of property tax — enumeration (identification of properties and maintenance of property records along with property details), property valuation and tax assessment, and tax billing and collection.
Technology has been a popular policy solution for improving enumeration. GIS-based mapping using satellite imagery and drones have been increasingly deployed to identify properties. However, such mapping exercises need to be accompanied by physical inspections conducted by municipal tax assessors; they also need to be repeated at regular intervals. But a perennial shortage of municipal staff, lack of requisite skills, and inadequate capacity building plague India’s municipalities. While human resource outsourcing can be a substitute, its efficiency is limited, as municipal assessors leverage institutional memory in a way that outsourced assessors cannot.
For valuation, the most common policy recommendation has been the capital valuation process, wherein a property is valued as per its stamp duty-linked ‘circle rate’ which is set and revised by the State revenue department at regular intervals. But most municipal bodies follow a valuation method wherein the ‘base rate’ is defined in rupees per sq ft per month, which is set by the municipality. Hence, tax buoyancy is determined by revisions to this base rate. But such revisions are infrequent compared to revisions in the stamp duty-linked circle rate. It was found that ‘base rate’ revisions did not take place across Bengaluru, Pune and Ghaziabad when there were no elected municipal councils. The link between municipal elections and tax performance is clear, at least for these three corporations. As delayed municipal elections are common, so is infrequent ‘base rate’ revision and lack of tax buoyancy.
Finally, for tax collections to be robust, collection efficiency needs to be strong. While extant recommendations include the adoption of both online collection as well as outsourcing the collection to external vendors, efficiency remains poor. Even more concerning is the difficulty in arriving at credible collection efficiency estimates due to the absence of properly maintained financial accounts.
To sum up, technology and process-based reforms are not enough for improving tax outcomes. Structural reforms encompassing more human resources, timely elections, and publicly available financial data play very important roles. It is high time that policy interventions broaden their focus to structural reforms for all aspects of urban governance and finance, including property tax.
Debarpita Roy is Lead-Research at the Centre for Public Policy on Housing and Habitat, NIUA, New Delhi. The views are personal.

stories.headline: Red to pink ball? MCC official clarifies how ICC’s new Test trial will work
stories.deck: Recent amendments by the International Cricket Council aim to combat time-wasting tactics in cricket, thereby accelerating the rhythm of matches for a more enjoyable spectator experience. Additionally, a possible pink-ball trial in Test formats will be negotiated in upcoming bilateral series. Umpires are charged with the responsibility of imposing penalties for slow over rates, illustrating…
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: With the game of cricket constantly evolving, the International Cricket Council (ICC) made a slew of changes to its playing conditions, which came into effect from Oct 1. Some of those changes included a pink-ball trial in Tests and time-wasting penalties.
Fraser Stewart, the Head of Cricket at Marylebone Cricket Club, opened up beyond the laws in a media interaction here on Monday.
Modern cricket is batter-friendly, and now the ICC playing conditions say five penalty runs for time-wasting. Is it a way of levelling the playing field?
The law has always been there. It’s just rarely been enacted, and I think now the ICC have said, right, we’re going to try to toughen up on this a bit. I think the more we can do to try to speed up play, the better it is. Otherwise, the public who pay a lot of money to watch cricket feel short-changed.
I think what the umpires try to do is to highlight to players that there are laws that cover this and if you waste time, it will catch up and there will be an in-game penalty of runs rather than a fine afterwards.
On pink-ball trial in day-time Tests...
That’s an ICC playing condition rather than a law of cricket. I believe, in a bilateral series, say, India playing Australia, it’s for them to agree among themselves for a particular game, are we going to use a pink ball?
Some people have thought you can start with a red ball and then when it gets a bit dark, you switch to pink. 
That’s not, as I understand it, what’s happening. Both need to agree and if they are happy to play with the pink ball, perhaps because they think that it’ll mean there can be more play after bad weather.
One big concern is the over rates. How does MCC act on this?
The laws do provide a remedy, both for batting and bowling sides. It’s for umpires to enforce those laws and, if they think the pace of play is too slow, whether it is the fielding captain or the batting side, and say, you’re on a warning; it will result in penalty runs.
But the umpires do need to enforce that, and be backed up by the match referees.

stories.headline: Para-shooters allege corruption in Asian Games selection
stories.deck: The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters alleged corruption and financial demands in the selection process. The shooters have sought an independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)…
stories.bodyText:
The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters alleged corruption and financial demands in the selection process.
The shooters have sought an independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) and its Shooting Technical Committee (STC).
In a representation submitted to the Director General of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Wednesday, the athletes alleged “illicit monetary extortion”, “brazen corruption” and violations of Sports Ministry guidelines.
The Para Asian Games are scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24.
Shooters allege 20 per cent demand
One of the most serious allegations made in the representation was that athletes were being asked to give 20 per cent of their government cash awards as a condition for being selected for the national team.
“Athletes are being coerced under severe duress into paying an illegal kickback of 20 per cent of their sanctioned government cash awards to designated committee office-bearers as a mandatory pre-condition for national team selection,” the representation alleged.
The shooters also alleged that international quota places were not allocated purely on rankings and performances. They claimed financial considerations played a role in deciding who received the available places.
According to their representation, two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores, ignoring Sports Ministry criteria and replacing an earlier selection panel without giving a recorded reason.
Sandeep Kumar alleges selection bias
P4 50m free pistol SH1 shooter Sandeep Kumar, ranked third in Asia, also questioned the selection decisions. He alleged that Rudrankksh Khandelwal, ranked 14th in Asia, was picked ahead of Akash, the Asian No. 1, and himself. Sandeep said he was “deeply aggrieved” by what he described as arbitrary decisions and violations of the selection rules.
The shooters also questioned the appointment of an individual as a technical expert and Director of Operations, alleging that the person had no record of competing in an official shooting event.
PCI rejects all allegations
PCI president 
Devendra Jhajharia
 strongly rejected the charges and said the team had been selected strictly according to the prescribed rules.
“The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry’s guidelines,” Jhajharia, a two-time Paralympics javelin gold-medallist, told PTI.
Jhajharia also rejected Sandeep’s allegation that he was left out to make way for a shooter who had links with the coach.
“Those are all false allegations,” Jhajharia said.
Ministry says grievances will be examined
A Sports Ministry source said genuine complaints raised by the para-shooters would be looked into. However, the source added that the Indian team for the Para Asian Games had already been finalised and could not be changed at this stage.
The shooters have also indicated that they could take the matter to court if their allegations are not addressed.
They said they may approach the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution, seeking a writ of mandamus and a court-monitored investigation into the selection process.

stories.headline: Karthik upsets Kamboj; Manish, Vaidehee reach quarters at Fenesta Open
stories.deck: The top five players in the women’s singles draw also booked their spots in the quarterfinals. Vaidehee Chaudhari defeated 16-year-old Ahaan Ahaan 6-4, 6-1, while Shruti Ahlawat beat Parthsarthi Mundhe 6-2, 6-2
stories.bodyText:
Pranav Karthik pulled off a major upset, rallying from a set down to knock out fourth seed Udit Kamboj in the second round of the 31st Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship here on Wednesday (October 7, 2026).
Kamboj won the first set 6-1 and was neck-and-neck with his younger rival in the second set, which went to a tie-break. Karthik won the tiebreak 7-3 and carried that momentum into the decider to win 1-6, 7-6 (7-3), 6-2 in 2 hours and 31 minutes.
“To be honest, I was thinking I was going to lose for sure after the horrible first set,” the 21-year-old from Tamil Nadu said after the win.
"I just kept serving well and maintaining my service games. And when it came to tiebreak, it's 50-50. Then I just pulled it off with 3-4 good points. When I pulled off the tiebreak, I got more confidence and started going for my shots.
"The first game of the third set is always important because you have to keep pushing through and keep the momentum because you don't want to give him the breathing space. And thankfully, I got the break in the first game and then I was able to run away with the match after that," he said.
Meanwhile, men’s top seed Manish Sureshkumar had little trouble defeating Lakshit Sood 6-0, 6-1 to advance to the quarterfinals. He was joined in the last eight by No. 6 seed Maan Kesharwani, No. 8 seed Rohan Mehra and Suraj Prabodh, who knocked out second seed Aditya Balsekar in the previous round on Tuesday.
The top five players in the women’s singles draw also booked their spots in the quarterfinals. Vaidehee Chaudhari defeated 16-year-old Ahaan Ahaan 6-4, 6-1, while Shruti Ahlawat beat Parthsarthi Mundhe 6-2, 6-2.
Third seed Akanksha Nitture also advanced, coming back after dropping the second set to defeat Yubrani Banerjee 6-1, 4-6, 6-1.
There was also a big upset in the Boys U-18 singles draw as top seed Praneel Sharma was bundled out 7-6 (7-4), 6-4 by Veer Jiten Madam. Fourth seed Om Ramesh Patel and fifth seed Aditya Mor won their third-round matches in straight sets to join Madam in the quarterfinals.
In the Girls U-18 event, top seed Savitha Bhuvaneswaran was stretched to the limit by 14th seed Aahida Singh. The two battled for 2 hours and 45 minutes before Singh was forced to retire, with Bhuvaneswaran leading 3-6, 7-6 (7-5), 3-0.
Bhuvaneswaran was joined by second seed Parthsarthi Mundhe and third seed Shreeniti Chowdhury in the quarterfinals.
